
## 2. Datasets

Each dataset loads once into a named object. Every question below starts from one of these objects.

### 2.1 whickham (package `mosaicData`)

1,314 women in a survey in Whickham, England. The variables are age, `smoker` and `outcome` (alive or dead 20 years later). The code makes the age groups in two ways, `case_when()` and `cut()`, and the next chunk checks that both give the same groups. The questions use `age_group`.

```{r}
#| label: data-whickham
whickham <- 
  |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    # way 1: case_when(), the first matching line wins
    age_group = case_when(
      age < 35 ~ "18-34",
      age < 45 ~ "35-44",
      age < 55 ~ "45-54",
      age < 65 ~ "55-64",
      age < 75 ~ "65-74",
      .default = "75+"
    ),
    # way 2: cut(), shorter, but you give the breaks and the labels
    age_group_cut = cut(age,
                        breaks = c(17, 34, 44, 54, 64, 74, 99),
                        labels = c("18-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65-74", "75+"))
  )
whickham |> head()
```

```{r}
#| label: check-age-groups
# both ways give the same six groups: 408, 216, 209, 238, 166 and 77 women
whickham |>
  count(age_group, age_group_cut)
```

### 2.4 world_exports (file in the course repository)

Export value in USD by country and product, average of 1998 to 2000. The product code follows the SITC classification, and its first digit gives the sector. The data come from the `economiccomplexity` package.

```{r}
#| label: data-exports
world_exports <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sergiouribe/Data_Visualization_Course_RSU/main/data/world_exports_1998_2000.csv",
  col_types = cols(product = col_character())
)
world_exports |> head()
```

## 3. Counting things

### 3.1 Pie or bars?

#### Question 1: How many women are in each age group?

Draw a pie chart of the age groups. Then rank the six slices from largest to smallest.

```{r}
#| label: q1
#| eval: false
whickham |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", fill = age_group)) +
  geom_bar(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +   # bends the bar into a circle
  theme_void()

```

### 3.6 Many parts of a whole: the treemap

#### Question 14: What did Latvia export in 1998 to 2000?

The first digit of the product code is the broad sector. Sum the export value by sector for Latvia (`lva`) and draw a treemap. Which sector has the largest area?

```{r}
#| label: q14
#| eval: false
world_exports |>
  filter(country == "lva") |> 
  # First digit of the product code (^ anchors to the start, \\d takes one digit)
  mutate(product_group = str_extract(product, "^\\d")) |>
  group_by(product_group) |> 
  summarise(value = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  arrange(desc(value)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(area = value, 
             fill = product_group, 
             label = product_group)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_text(colour = "white", reflow = TRUE) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

```{r}
world_exports |>
  filter(country == "lva") |> 
  # First digit of the product code (^ anchors to the start, \\d takes one digit)
  mutate(product_group = str_extract(product, "^\\d")) |>
  group_by(product_group) |> 
  summarise(value = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  arrange(desc(value)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = value, 
             fill = product_group, 
             label = product_group)) +
  geom_bar() +
  # geom_treemap_text(colour = "white", reflow = TRUE) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

**Your finding:**
